description: Create web-based user interfaces with Python. The nice way.

sources.entry: nicegui - An easy-to-use, Python-based UI framework, which shows up in your web browser.

summary.one_liner: NiceGUI is a Python framework for building browser-based graphical user interfaces, with buttons, dialogs, charts, 3D scenes and more, without writing HTML or JavaScript.
summary.what_it_does: NiceGUI lets you write a web UI in plain Python: you declare elements such as labels, buttons, inputs, sliders, file uploads, and tables, and they appear in the browser. The README describes higher-level elements for plots and charts, 3D scenes, virtual joysticks, image annotation, tree views, and embedded video and audio. It supports data binding, refreshable functions, timers that refresh data at intervals (even every 10 ms), notifications, dialogs, menus, per-user and general persistence, custom routes, and keyboard shortcuts. The app can run as a web server accessed by a browser or in a native desktop-window mode, and it reloads the page when code changes. The README says it is built on FastAPI, Uvicorn, and Vue/Quasar, with socket.io for communication.
use_cases: build a micro web app in Python
create a dashboard for live data
control or monitor a robotics project
build a smart home control panel
tune machine learning parameters with a GUI
prototype a desktop-style interface from Python
how_to_run: Write main.py with: from nicegui import ui; ui.label('Hello NiceGUI!'); ui.run()
Alternatively: docker run -p 8080:8080 zauberzeug/nicegui (runs the documentation app)
notable: Pure Python UI definition; the browser frontend is handled by the framework
Native mode can open a desktop window instead of a browser tab
Backend-first design with a single uvicorn worker and an outbox that batches UI updates
Ships llms.md reference file for building projects with AI assistants
Available on PyPI, Docker, conda-forge, and GitHub
caveats: The README does not list platform limits or paid tiers
Uses a single uvicorn worker, so it does not scale across processes via multiple workers
keywords: make a simple gui in python
